findings.evidence: The construction rotates v_1 to e_{a_1} while fixing v_1's orthogonal complement. An orthogonal map fixing that complement pointwise must send v_1 to ±v_1, making the stated rotation impossible for v_1=(e_1+e_2)/sqrt(2), a_1=2. It must instead fix the common perpendicular of v_1 and e_{a_1}. D(a) also needs an explicit closed-hemisphere frame definition allowing zero boundary pivots. Hatcher, Vector Bundles & K-Theory, Proposition 1.17, printed pp.33–34, supplies the correct continuous rotation, fiber trivialization, frame domain, and complex variant; the complete relevant argument was read. The assigned consumer directly uses this characteristic-ball construction. Repair the published proof against that argument; the theorem itself remains source-supported.
